cityWatch.label: CITY WATCH
cityWatch.text: A Bengaluru restaurant was fined ₹10,000 after charging a customer ₹15 for a branded takeaway bag, the consumer forum ruled.

lead.headline: ₹2,321 CRORE TO WHITE-TOP 88 BENGALURU ROADS; ₹487 CRORE CLEARED FOR ORR LINK
lead.deck: The Karnataka government approved a fourth-phase white-topping project for 88 city roads and funding for a Central Silk Board–K R Pura Outer Ring Road link.
paragraphs: The state approved ₹2,321 crore to white-top 88 Bengaluru roads in the project's fourth phase. The package includes walkable footpaths, redesigned junctions, lighting and utility works.
A separate ₹487-crore allocation was approved for the Central Silk Board to K R Pura ORR link, a key eastern Bengaluru corridor.

image.alt: Officials inspect white-topping work on Hennur-Bagalur Road in Bengaluru.
image.caption: File photo: officials inspect white-topping work on Hennur-Bagalur Road. The Bengaluru Live.

sidebarStory.headline: INDIA AND JAPAN AGREE TO DEEPEN DEFENCE COOPERATION AND HOLD LIVE-FIRE DRILLS
sidebarStory.subhead: The agreement includes Japanese missile training at Indian ranges and closer defence-industry work.
paragraphs: After talks in Tokyo, the two governments agreed to expand military and defence-industry cooperation, including allowing Japanese troops to conduct live-fire missile training at Indian firing ranges during future joint exercises.
The ministers also discussed technology and equipment cooperation under a “design with Japan, make in India” framework.

image.alt: India and Japan foreign and defence ministers at a joint press conference in Tokyo on November 19, 2026.
image.caption: India and Japanese ministers meet in Tokyo. Rodrigo Reyes Marin/Pool Photo via AP.

stories.headline: BENGALURU'S FIRST CHIEF POLICE COMMISSIONER SETS OUT PRIORITIES FOR FIVE NEW ZONES
paragraphs: R Hithendra, the city's first Chief Commissioner of Police, said five territorial commissionerates would be made operational as soon as possible.
The new structure divides Bengaluru into North, South, East, West and Central zones, with a separate traffic commissioner.

stories.headline: BLUE LINE COMPLETES A 6-KM TRIAL RUN IN LATEST TEST PHASE
paragraphs: The Bengaluru Metro Blue Line completed a trial run covering six kilometres, according to a report in the city's November 20 morning roundup.
The airport corridor is a closely watched project for commuters travelling between eastern Bengaluru and Kempegowda International Airport.

stories.headline: 24 VENTURE FUNDS ANNOUNCE ₹1,050 CRORE FOR DEEPTECH STARTUPS
paragraphs: Twenty-four venture capital firms announced investments worth ₹1,050 crore in more than 68 deeptech startups at the Bengaluru Tech Summit.
Karnataka's IT minister said the state's startup ecosystem had raised $4.4 billion this year, accounting for 43 per cent of technology investment in India, figures cited at the event.

stories.headline: MODI CHALLENGES INDIA INC TO TURN TAX RELIEF INTO HIGHER PAY AND MORE JOBS
paragraphs: Addressing FICCI's annual convention, Prime Minister Narendra Modi asked companies whether lower corporate taxes had translated into stronger hiring and higher employee wages.
He urged industry to invest more in agriculture and allied sectors and to suggest further reforms for economic growth.

stories.headline: INDIAN TROOPS KILL MILITANT COMMANDER AFTER VILLAGE SIEGE IN SOUTHERN KASHMIR
paragraphs: Government forces killed Mohammed Lateef Bhat in Kulgam district after security personnel surrounded villages following an ambush that wounded three paramilitary soldiers, police said.
Residents described hardship during searches and detentions. The Associated Press said it could not independently verify all details of the operation.

stories.headline: TVK MLA V S BABU DIES AFTER PROLONGED HOSPITALISATION
paragraphs: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam legislator V S Babu has died after a prolonged hospital stay, according to the Times of India's November 19 live coverage.
The death marks a major loss for the party and its supporters in Tamil Nadu.

stories.headline: RESTAURANT WASTE OIL IS BEING TURNED INTO BIOFUEL
paragraphs: A Bengaluru initiative is collecting used cooking oil from restaurants and converting the waste into biofuel, giving eateries a route to divert spent oil from unsafe reuse.
The effort connects the city's food businesses with a local fuel-making operation, according to Deccan Herald coverage in the morning roundup.

stories.headline: GOVINDARAJANAGAR HOSPITAL TO BECOME A JAYADEVA CARDIAC CARE CENTRE
paragraphs: The Govindarajanagar hospital is to be converted into a cardiac-care centre under the Jayadeva Institute, expanding specialist heart services in western Bengaluru.
The move was among the city health developments reported in Thursday's Bengaluru news roundup.

stories.headline: CHANGENOW HUB OPENS IN BENGALURU TO TAKE CLIMATE STARTUPS GLOBAL
paragraphs: The ChangeNOW Hub launched at the Bengaluru Tech Summit to help Indian climate-focused startups expand internationally.
Organisers said Bengaluru's technology ecosystem and focus on climate and urban sustainability made it a natural base for the initiative.

stories.headline: INDIA A OPEN THEIR RISING STARS CAMPAIGN AGAINST NEPAL TODAY
paragraphs: India A begin their DP World Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign against Nepal in Doha on Friday, with a young squad led by high-profile prospects.
The BCCI match centre lists the fixture for November 20 at West End Park International Stadium.

stories.headline: DHANUSH'S “OM” TOPS HIS PREVIOUS FILM IN ADVANCE BOOKINGS
paragraphs: Dhanush's upcoming film OM: Chapter 1 – Udhiram crossed ₹7 crore in worldwide opening-day advance bookings, including block seats, as of midday Thursday.
The film, also starring Mammootty and Sai Pallavi, surpassed the advance-booking total of Raayan, NDTV reported.

stories.headline: MOSTLY CLOUDY IN BENGALURU; NO RAIN EXPECTED

paragraphs: The forecast for Bengaluru on Friday is mostly cloudy, with temperatures between 22°C and 29°C and no rain expected.
